chat.text: For the new people joining, please help with the meeting mintues: https://notes.ietf.org/notes-ietf-127-opsawg

chat.author: Benoît Claise
chat.text:
@Victor, regarding "your" draft, I am right that there are no more open issues from https://github.com/vlopezalvarez/draft-contreras-opsawg-scheduling-oam-tests/issues.
This is the right github?

chat.author: Titouan Soulard
chat.text: Is the idea to allow YANG models to evolve independently of the drafts / RFCs? It seems difficult to keep up consistent commit id to draft revision mapping.

chat.author: Mahesh Jethanandani
chat.text: Hi @Titouan, the idea is that the RFC will keep a pointer to a IANA registry which in turn will point to the version of the YANG module that should be considered.

chat.author: Michael Richardson
chat.text: (deleted)

chat.author: Michael Richardson
chat.text: (I think that this new registry could be folded into the existing YANG Modules Names registry, if the experiment concludes successfully)

chat.author: Titouan Soulard
chat.text: That's what I see now, the question was too early. I wonder why it is more difficult to diff YANG than draft text. I believe now many people already work on I.-D.s in Git before publishing through IETF processes, so diff-ing seems a more general problem, I wonder if YANG is so different. If all of this was already answer on the mailing or in the draft, I'd be happy that you refuse to answer my question here and tell me to read BTW. I am discovering the draft just now.

chat.author: Mahesh Jethanandani
chat.text: Diffing is not the main reason. The idea is that YANG module is code and it needs to be treated as such.

chat.author: Titouan Soulard
chat.text: Is there history on handling such code-like objects from IETF or IANA? Or is this a new idea for YANG, (since we handle a lot of YANG nowadays)?

chat.author: Mahesh Jethanandani
chat.text: What that means is that code is easier to review in a SCM, update and publish a new version of the module.

chat.author: Titouan Soulard
chat.text: Yes, I do get it, it seems reasonable. My understanding of the presentation was wrong, I thought it was "YANG is hard to diff as text".

chat.author: Pedro Martinez-Julia
chat.text: Please, focus camera on the speaker.

chat.author: Per Andersson
chat.text: @meetecho please focus camera on the speaker

chat.author: Michael Richardson
chat.text:
I'm not yet sure if the registry has a version column, in which there is a value "latest", or if there is a mechanism by which IANA can be asked for the latest entry, and it produces the one with the highest "version"
The LATER probably prefers to be a moving part, but it could be a static entry updated when new entries are added.

chat.author: Joe Clarke
chat.text: As a contributor, I like the idea of pointing to the latest published YANG module.  That said, I think perhaps a MAJOR change to a YANG module (non-backwards-compat change) should trigger bis and then you'd have a new RFC with a new pointer.

chat.author: Pedro Martinez-Julia
chat.text: @meetecho Focus camera on the speaker.

chat.author: Benoît Claise
chat.text: This draft is at the intersection of OPSAWG (next to provenance, NETMOD (YANG), and NMOP (ietf-nmop-yang-message-broker-message-key as a use case). Like Joe, don't care too much about the WG.

chat.author: Mahesh Jethanandani
chat.text: Suggest we close this with NETMOD. As Joe mentioned by Joe, there is another "normalization" draft in NETMOD that will have to be reconciled with.

chat.author: Ana Mendez
chat.text: Indeed, we will check this

chat.author: Joe Clarke
chat.text: Yeah.  I just want to avoid the back and forth that happened with prov.  I can certainly get behind this work in NETMOD.

chat.author: Joe Clarke
chat.text: Can remote people hear Paolo?

chat.author: Per Andersson
chat.text: yes

chat.author: Joe Clarke
chat.text: I have a question on ordered elements.  If you just do 1 and 3 and skip 2 is that in and of itself useful?  You'd at least know the order that 1 comes before 3.

chat.author: Holger Keller
chat.text: @Joe There are implementations that allow to configure export of 1 and 3, but not 2. i am currently not aware of a use case, but maybe someone else has one. yet, this case needs to be thought of.

chat.author: Benoît Claise
chat.text: @Joe, " the order that 1 comes before 3" Yes that's all you know from a collector point of view.

chat.author: Joe Clarke
chat.text: Right.  Could that additional knowledge still be valuable even if you don't know that they are actually position 1 and 3?

chat.author: Paul Aitken
chat.text: If the collector receives two items, it wouldn't know whether they are 1 and 2, or 1 and 3 with 2 missing, or 1 and N with lots missing.

chat.author: Joe Clarke
chat.text: Right.  But they would know the outer layer vs. the inner one.  Just asking if there is an operational use case for that.  It's more for curiosity given Benoit's points about hardware challenges around adding indices.

chat.author: Paul Aitken
chat.text: The hardware challenge is more in implementing export of structured data.

chat.author: Mohamed Boucadair
chat.text: Thanks Doug for working on this. This covers a gap that was identified in RFC9887.

chat.author: Thomas Graf
chat.text: Looking forward that the SSH public key distribution via Tacacs+ is adopted at OPSAWG
